section_summary: This section details United States and Allied occupation policies concerning Japanese science, technology, and patent rights between October 1945 and May 1948. It documents persistent diplomatic negotiations with the United Kingdom and Australia over access to Japanese scientific and industrial research, the dispatch of investigating missions, and the release of findings from the Dr. Roger Adams survey. In addition, it covers domestic American protests by the Federation of American Scientists against restrictions on nuclear physics and cyclotron destruction, alongside a detailed SCAP analysis of post-war Japanese public and media attitudes toward science. Finally, interdepartmental deliberations within SWNCC and SANACC establish formal mechanisms to coordinate investigations under SCAP authority and facilitate the public dissemination of non-military Japanese technology.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of constituent letter from Professor Wheeler P. Davey requesting scientific information on Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits constituent correspondence concerning Japanese scientific data to the Secretary of State for reply.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of constituent inquiry regarding Japanese scientific research

subfiles.about: Request for further information from Professor Wheeler P. Davey regarding Japanese scientists and research institutes.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Davey's letter and solicits additional data on Japanese scientists G. Asahara, Kotaro Honda, and research institutes.
subfiles.title: Department of State reply regarding G. Asahara and Kotaro Honda

subfiles.about: Transmittal of British Embassy letter regarding Japanese scientific research inquiries.
subfiles.summary: Forwards British Embassy letter and clarifies General McCoy's statements regarding intelligence exchanges and scientific information in Japan.
subfiles.title: British Request for Information

subfiles.about: Informal British inquiry on US willingness to disclose Japanese scientific research and accept FEC commissions of enquiry.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether the United States would disclose Japanese scientific research without qualification and recognize FEC inquiry rights.
subfiles.title: British inquiry regarding Japanese scientific research and FEC missions

subfiles.about: State Department analysis of British proposals on Japanese scientific research and FEC inquiry missions.
subfiles.summary: Recommends Army and Navy decision on disclosing scientific research and accepts in principle FEC missions under SCAP authority.
subfiles.title: Comments on British request for scientific information

subfiles.about: State Department views on disclosing Japanese scientific data and FEC missions to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Concludes that disclosing scientific data requires military decision and that FEC inquiry missions to Japan are permissible in principle.
subfiles.title: British Request for Information

subfiles.about: Reply regarding British access to SCAP investigations into non-military Japanese scientific research.
subfiles.summary: Informs Sansom that SCAP conducts non-military scientific inquiries and can honor requests from British military representatives in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Inquiries into Japanese scientific research

subfiles.about: Interim State Department reply regarding British requests for Japanese scientific research information.
subfiles.summary: States that providing an explicit answer to British Foreign Office queries regarding Japanese scientific research requires further delay.
subfiles.title: Interim reply regarding scientific research in Japan

subfiles.about: British request for comprehensive assurances regarding access to Japanese scientific research.
subfiles.summary: Reiterates Foreign Office instructions seeking an unqualified assurance that all available Japanese scientific research information will be disclosed.
subfiles.title: Request for assurances on Japanese scientific research

subfiles.about: Report on intelligence liaison formula resolving the British scientific information request and withdrawing SWNCC 216/4.
subfiles.summary: Reports that British and American intelligence officers agreed on specific liaison procedures and recommends recalling and destroying SWNCC 216/4.
subfiles.title: British Request for Information on Japanese Scientific Research (SWNCC 216/4)

subfiles.about: British proposal to dispatch two civilian scientists to Japan on a joint investigation of academic research.
subfiles.summary: Proposes sending two British civilian academic scientists to Japan alongside American counterparts to examine non-military academic research, requesting US agreement and logistic assistance.
subfiles.title: Proposal for joint civilian scientific mission to Japan (Ref: G.8/-/47)

subfiles.about: Routing of Federation of American Scientists inquiry regarding Japanese nuclear physics restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Higinbotham's letter regarding Japanese nuclear physics restrictions to the Division of International Science Policy for advice.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of FAS letter from W. A. Higinbotham

subfiles.about: FAS protest against cyclotron destruction and inquiry into restrictions on Japanese nuclear research and scientific interchange.
subfiles.summary: Questions the prohibition on Japanese nuclear physics, the destruction of cyclotrons, and restrictions preventing scientific interchange and publication sharing.
subfiles.title: Inquiry regarding restrictions on Japanese nuclear physics and scientific interchange

subfiles.about: Guidance on replying to FAS regarding nuclear physics controls and international atomic energy policy.
subfiles.summary: Advises consulting General Hilldring's office regarding occupation controls while explaining occupation security requirements and international atomic energy policies.
subfiles.title: Suggestions for replying to FAS letter on Japanese science policy

subfiles.about: Explanation of FEC policies on Japanese atomic research, scientific periodicals, and travel restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Informs FAS that the Far Eastern Commission unanimously banned Japanese atomic research, outlines procedures for sending scientific periodicals via SCAP, and notes pending consideration of personal travel.
subfiles.title: Reply to FAS regarding Japanese atomic research and scientific interchange

subfiles.about: British request for a decision on the proposed joint civilian scientific mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Inquires whether the US Government can concur with the British memorandum of March 11 proposing a joint scientific mission.
subfiles.title: British inquiry on proposed scientific mission to Japan (Ref. G8/-/26)

subfiles.about: US decision to submit the question of Allied scientific investigation in Japan to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Conveys US sympathy with British scientific proposals but states an FEC policy decision is required, which the US will submit.
subfiles.title: US reply regarding British participation in Japanese scientific investigation

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment that FAS obtained FEC regulations and found occupation atomic policy sensible.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Schuler's letter, stating FAS obtained official FEC regulations directly and found the January 30 atomic policy sensible.
subfiles.title: FAS acknowledgment of FEC atomic energy regulations

subfiles.about: Transmittal of SCAP CI&E Media Analysis report on Japanese attitudes toward science.
subfiles.summary: Forwards copies of a SCAP Civil Information and Education Section report analyzing Japanese press and magazine commentary on science.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Report Concerning the Japanese Attitude Toward Science (Despatch No. 1319)

subfiles.about: Detailed survey of post-war Japanese magazine articles discussing scientific development, technology, atomic power, and public health.
subfiles.from: Civil Information and Education Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Analyzes post-war Japanese periodicals showing deep concern over the nation's lagging scientific development and insufficient government funding compared to the United States. Covers discussions on the need for scientific thinking, industrial modernization, peaceful applications of atomic energy, public health deficiencies, and popular scientific education.
subfiles.title: Publications Analysis No. 96: The Japanese Attitude Toward Science
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: State Department recommendation to provide the British Embassy with reports from the Roger Adams scientific mission.
subfiles.summary: Recommends providing reports of the Dr. Roger Adams mission to the British Embassy to resolve legitimate British grievances.
subfiles.title: British Desire for Scientific Mission to Japan

subfiles.about: Conversation with British Counselor H. A. Graves regarding British demands for scientific access and Adams group reports.
subfiles.summary: Records British Counselor Graves's formal representations demanding reports of the Dr. Roger Adams mission and renewing requests to send British investigators to Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Scientific Mission to Japan

subfiles.about: Informal British aide-mémoire detailing the background of British requests and requesting full results of the Roger Adams mission.
subfiles.summary: Outlines the history of British requests for Japanese scientific data and asserts Britain should receive full results of the Roger Adams mission.
subfiles.title: Scientific Mission (British Embassy Informal Memorandum)

subfiles.about: Urgent submission of State Department policy paper on Japanese technology to SANACC without subcommittee referral.
subfiles.summary: Submits State Department policy paper on investigating Japanese technology, requesting direct SANACC consideration without reference to the Far Eastern Subcommittee.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Policy Paper 'Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology'

subfiles.about: Draft submittal requesting SANACC consideration of the Japanese technology investigation program.
subfiles.summary: Draft version of memorandum submitting the policy paper on Japanese technology to SANACC without subcommittee referral.
subfiles.title: Draft Memorandum for the Secretary, SANACC: Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology

subfiles.about: Formal State Department submittal of Japanese technology paper for direct SANACC consideration.
subfiles.summary: Submits the policy paper on Japanese technology to SANACC with a request for action without referral to SFE.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Secretary, SANACC: Paper entitled 'Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology'

subfiles.about: Submission of policy paper on Japanese technology with handwritten instructions bypassing SFE.
subfiles.summary: Submits policy paper on Japanese technology with marginal notes requesting direct SANACC action without submission to SFE.
subfiles.title: Submittal of paper entitled 'Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology'

subfiles.about: Draft report outlining policy and conclusions for admitting Allied technical investigators into Japan under SCAP.
subfiles.from: State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Committee for the Far East
subfiles.summary: Recommends sending up to twenty-five technical investigators from FEC countries to Japan under SCAP control, supervised by John C. Green.
subfiles.title: Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology (Draft Report by SANACC for the Far East)

subfiles.about: Detailed compilation of directives, executive orders, statutory authorities, and diplomatic cables on enemy technology and patents.
subfiles.summary: Details background authorities regarding enemy technology, quoting SWNCC 52/7, SWNCC 369 on Japanese patents, and Executive Orders 9568 and 9604 establishing the Publication Board. Reviews Department of Commerce efforts to send investigators, SCAP cable exchanges opposing unilateral action, and Public Law 380 patent provisions.
subfiles.title: Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology: Appendix 'A' (Facts Bearing on the Problem)

subfiles.about: Discussion justifying an Allied technical investigation program in Japan based on German precedents and European reconstruction needs.
subfiles.summary: Discusses the rationale for investigating Japanese technology along lines established in Germany, recommending Commerce Department management under SCAP control and FEC participation to support post-war industrial and European economic rehabilitation.
subfiles.title: Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology: Appendix 'B' (Discussion)

subfiles.about: Transmittal of US policy statement and SCAP conditions for FEC technical investigations in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits US policy paper and statement of conditions established by SCAP governing foreign technical investigations in Japan to General McCoy.
subfiles.title: Policy statement regarding access to Japanese technical and scientific information in Japan (SC-280 Series)

subfiles.about: US policy authorizing FEC member governments access to pre-1946 Japanese technical processes.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes FEC member governments access to pre-1946 Japanese technical processes between July 1, 1948 and March 31, 1949, requiring full disclosure to SCAP.
subfiles.title: Access to Japanese Technical and Scientific Information in Japan (Policy Statement)

subfiles.about: Nine administrative conditions established by SCAP governing foreign technical investigators in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Details nine SCAP conditions governing technical investigators, including limiting representatives to twenty-five individual experts, excluding dependents, and providing logistic support on revenue basis.
subfiles.title: Statement to be Made by U.S. Representative Regarding U.S. Proposal on SC-280 Series
subfiles.to: United States Representative, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Transmittal of memorandum of information on Japanese technology investigation to SANACC and JCS.
subfiles.summary: Circulates a memorandum of information regarding the SANACC 216 series to SANACC committee members and the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Memorandum of Information on Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology (SANACC 216 Series)

subfiles.about: Detailed background review of SANACC 216, military security objections, Australian FEC pressure, and SCAP conditions.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes negotiations over Japanese technology investigation policies, detailing JCS security concerns, Australian initiatives in the FEC, SCAP's conditions, and rejection of reciprocity demands. Concludes that SCAP's administrative controls satisfy military security concerns, allowing US acceptance of a modified Australian policy.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Information: Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology

subfiles.about: Request for Far Eastern Subcommittee review of Australian FEC proposals and US counterproposals.
subfiles.summary: Requests immediate subcommittee consideration of SANACC 216/5, 216/6, the Australian FEC proposal, and a proposed US counterproposal.
subfiles.title: Scientific and Technical Investigations in Japan (SANACC 216/5, 216/6)

subfiles.about: Australian proposal granting United Nations members access to pre-surrender Japanese technical processes.
subfiles.summary: Proposes that United Nations representatives be permitted access to and copies of pre-surrender Japanese technical and scientific processes upon request to SCAP.
subfiles.title: Appendix 'A': Australian Proposal Regarding Access to Japanese Technical and Scientific Processes

subfiles.about: US draft counterproposal restricting access to non-military pre-1946 processes and requiring SCAP disclosure.
subfiles.summary: Proposes allowing United Nations access to pre-1946 non-military processes, with SCAP coordinating visits and disseminating all gathered data.
subfiles.title: Appendix 'B': United States Draft Counterproposal on Technical and Scientific Investigations

subfiles.about: Secretariat note circulating State Department study on Japanese technology to SANACC and JCS.
subfiles.from: W. A. Schulgen, V. L. Lowrance, J. P. Gardiner
subfiles.summary: Circulates State Department study on Japanese technology to SANACC and the Joint Chiefs of Staff as an urgent matter.
subfiles.title: SANACC 216/5: Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology (Note by the Secretaries)

subfiles.about: Circulated State Department study on sending Allied technical investigators to Japan under SCAP control.
subfiles.summary: Circulates State Department study recommending that up to twenty-five technical investigators from Far Eastern Commission countries be permitted to investigate Japanese technology under SCAP supervision.
subfiles.title: SANACC 216/5: Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology (Enclosure)
